findings.reason: the role scoping is the sentence the implementer would most plausibly drop, and no arm fails when it is dropped, so the gate as written admits a refusal that breaks review promotion broadly.
findings.text: §5 scopes the refusal to "an implementation run", but every arm of the done-when is an implementation-shaped run, so a guard keyed on `--gate passed` alone (no role test) passes all eight arms while refusing or fetching for every composed-review promotion: a composed review's pointer carries `head` equal to the head it reviewed (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:641`), which is a node's worktree head and not on the primary branch, and the plain complete path already handles review runs at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3154`. The missing arm is a review-role run with a head off the branch that still promotes, which is the negative control for the role scoping — without it the arm set cannot distinguish the stated mechanism from the unscoped one

response_events.note: §5's done-when adds a review-role arm: a composed review with an off-branch head promotes with --gate passed and runs no fetch, with gate-only keying as its control

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` "near line 944" is `_integration_ref` at 944–972, `reckon/crew/merge.py` 157–180 is the `promotion.complete_dry_run` call inside `require_promotable_head`, `promotion.complete_dry_run` exists at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:895`, and "Nothing in `reckon/` fetches today" holds (no `git fetch` in `reckon/`; the only `fetch` hits are the model-catalogue HTTP fetch in `reckon/crew/model_catalogue.py`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the new `--gate passed` conditioning in `plan.html:60` is scoped in the Deliverable to "an implementation run", but no done-when arm exercises that role scoping, so an implementation keyed on the gate verdict alone passes every arm.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate logs land "under the run directory", which is `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/` on shared storage, not a node-local temp path; the new test file sits in `tests/`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test file and the planned function are named by the behaviour (`test_a_plain_complete_refuses_an_unmerged_head.py`), and the section carries no ticket numbers, plan labels or changelog prose into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the three checks hold: the Why's root cause (a plain complete promotes without an ancestry check) matches the cited nova-39/nova-8a reports and the code as it stands; the mechanism (fetch, then ancestry against the fetched ref, refusing on unmerged head or failed fetch or missing ref) produces each arm of the done-when; and the mechanism names its production caller, "the plain `crew complete` path in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`", which is the path that reaches `crew_module.complete` at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3257` and is distinct from the `promotion.complete_dry_run` guard list `crew merge --run` shares.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable (one refusal in the plain complete path) and its newly added arms measure that one refusal's gate conditioning, not a second feature.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5 is the upstream s6 and s7 both declare in `plan-section-depends-on` (`{"s6":["...#s5"],"s7":["...#s5"]}`), §6's closing sentence says it waits on this section, and §7 calls the fetch-and-check function §5 adds, so the relationship the new content creates is declared and points the right way.
